s01.setup: A ferry carrying the harbour's lamp oil has stalled at the dock, and a crowd is waiting on the quay.
s01.line: That engine has not purred like that in years.
s01.lit: The oil is ashore and the harbour lamp catches. The water glows back.

o.R: Open the engine and fix it, with oily hands and no one to ask for help
o.I: Work out from tides and wind why it stalled, though the answer may come too late
o.A: Paint a big board so the crowd knows what is happening, with an hour to finish
o.S: Keep the waiting children calm and busy, even if you miss the repair

s01.clue: The lamplighter once stayed up all night with me taking this engine apart. Oil to her elbows.

s02.setup: The old stone bridge has a cracked arch, and lantern-bearers need to cross before midnight.
s02.line: My father laid that arch. It is good to see it lit again.
s02.lit: Lantern-bearers stream across, and the old arch glows.

o.R: Fit the new planks by hand in the cold, getting every joint tight before midnight
o.I: Find out why this arch cracked, even if it takes all night of measuring
o.A: Sketch a new arch shape for the bridge, though most first ideas get thrown out
o.E: Lead the repair team, and face the blame if it goes wrong

s02.clue: She measured every arch of this bridge twice. Said a bridge should be understood before it is trusted.

s03.setup: The tower clock that tells the lane when to light its lamps has gone wrong.
s03.line: Right on dusk, and the whole lane is ready.
s03.lit: The tower strikes dusk. Every window in the lane lights at once.

o.R: Climb the tower and follow the broken gear by hand, in a dusty, cramped space
o.I: Study the pattern of missed chimes, though it may take days to spot the cause
o.A: Repaint the clock face so it is easier to read, even if some liked the old one
o.C: Write up a step-by-step repair checklist, redoing it as things change

s03.clue: She taught me to read the clock's gears, then sketched the whole tower on the back of her hand.

s04.setup: Apples are ripening faster than the village can press them.
s04.line: Sweet air, sweet juice, and now a lamp. A good evening's work.
s04.lit: The orchard is calm. Its lamp swings among the apple trees.

o.R: Run the press and keep it humming all day
o.I: Test apple blends to work out why one tastes best
o.S: Teach visiting children to make juice through games
o.E: Sell the fresh juice to passers-by on the village road

s04.clue: Last autumn she pressed apples with us from dawn, and sold the first jars herself.

s05.setup: Fog has settled on the mountain pass, the signal lamp is dim, and travellers are feeling their way through.
s05.line: Nobody was left behind in my pass tonight.
s05.lit: A thin gold line cuts the fog. The pass has its light, and the way is clear.

o.R: Mend the dim signal lamp alone on the ridge, in freezing wind
o.I: Map where the fog is thickest to find a safer path, standing still in the cold
o.S: Lift the lost travellers' spirits on a long, cold walk
o.C: Count everyone through the pass so no one is left behind, even as people grow impatient

s05.clue: In the fog she walked at the back of the line, counting every traveller through.

s06.setup: The bazaar opens at dusk. Your borrowed stall is empty, apart from a strange old machine in the corner.
s06.line: A lit lamp is the best sign a stall can have.
s06.lit: The bazaar glows, and a lamp hangs overhead, warm as a cup of tea.

o.R: Build a sturdy stall frame from the plan, working fast as the light fades
o.I: Examine the old machine to learn its use, though it may turn out to be junk
o.E: Win over the passing buyers, knowing some will walk away
o.C: Label the shelves so buyers find things fast, before the doors open

s06.clue: She once bargained for a whole bazaar's lamp oil and left every trader smiling.

s07.setup: A wide river blocks the road, and tired lamp-bearers have stopped to rest on the bank.
s07.line: The river will carry your lamp's light all the way to the sea.
s07.lit: The group is rested and ready for the crossing. The lamp's reflection drifts downstream.

o.R: Build a raft from whatever wood is nearby, with sore arms and wet feet
o.A: Dream up a new boat shape for the crossing, though it may not float the first time
o.S: Care for the tired travellers through the night while others plan the crossing
o.E: Run the camp meeting and push for a decision, even if some people are unhappy

s07.clue: She spent a night with the tired travellers here, then drew them the way across at dawn.

s08.setup: The great loom that weaves the banners is creaking, and market day is near.
s08.line: Every banner in town will glow a little brighter tomorrow.
s08.lit: Banners hang above the street, and a lamp lights behind them.

o.R: Repair the creaking loom, crawling under it with tools for hours
o.A: Design a banner pattern for the town, knowing not everyone will like it
o.S: Coach a nervous new weaver, even though progress is slow and they may give up
o.C: Track the cloth rolls for market day, recounting whenever the totals don't match

s08.clue: She sat at my loom for a week and wove a banner nobody forgot.

s09.setup: A group needs to reach the cliff top by evening, and the glassy rock is glowing strangely.
s09.line: From up here the whole road looks like a string of stars.
s09.lit: The highest lamp is lit. The cliffs shine like glass for miles.

o.R: Rope down a short stretch to test the rock, which is slow, tiring work
o.A: Draw a picture map of the glowing cliff for the climbers, redrawing it as the light shifts
o.E: Lead the climbers to the top, though some will grumble at your choices
o.C: Check every harness against the safety list while others start climbing first

s09.clue: She roped down these cliffs to check the old lamps, and mapped how the light moves.

s10.setup: A load of salt has spilled, two traders are arguing, and a crowd is gathering.
s10.line: Quiet market, warm lamp. The best kind of night.
s10.lit: The market hums, and its lamp is lit above the stalls.

o.R: Haul the salt sacks off the road and stack them, heavy work in the heat
o.S: Calm the gathering crowd and listen to each person's worry, which takes a while
o.E: Settle the argument with a deal both traders accept, though neither is fully happy
o.C: Weigh what salt is left so each trader's loss is clear, with the crowd shouting nearby

s10.clue: When the traders quarrelled, she weighed the salt herself, and then settled it.

s11.setup: A clear night is coming, and visitors are climbing the hill to watch the stars come out.
s11.line: The sky has been waiting for this.
s11.lit: The hill lamp lifts its light into the dark, and the sky answers.

o.I: Chart the stars and wonder what is out there
o.A: Paint the night sky and notice how it changes
o.S: Welcome the visitors and help each one find a good spot to look
o.E: Recruit new members for the stargazing club

s11.clue: She came up here to watch the stars, then taught the village children their names.

s12.setup: The garden that grows the sweet lamp-herbs is overgrown, and the season is turning.
s12.line: The herbs will sleep well tonight.
s12.lit: The beds breathe, and the lamp smells of rain and mint.

o.I: Test soils and seeds to grow healthier plants
o.A: Shape the garden so it feels peaceful to walk in
o.S: Show children how to care for the plants through stories
o.C: Label each herb bed so nothing gets mixed up

s12.clue: She kept this garden's herb beds in order for a season and tasted every leaf.

s13.setup: An old printing press has been found in a cellar, and the whole quarter wants it working.
s13.line: Ink and light. They go together.
s13.lit: Ink and paper fill the quarter, and a lamp lights above the cellar door.

o.I: Investigate how the old press works, reading faded notes that may lead nowhere
o.A: Design a new letter style for the press, then redo it if people can't read it
o.E: Launch a new newspaper for the quarter, at the risk it does not sell
o.C: Proofread each page before printing, starting over whenever a mistake slips through

s13.clue: She read every page of the old press's notes and redrew its letters by hand.

s14.setup: Travellers have come to rest before the next leg of the road, and some are unwell tonight.
s14.line: Steady light. They can rest now.
s14.lit: The house settles into calm. A steady lamp burns in the window.

o.I: Test the water to find what is making people ill, with many tests that show nothing
o.S: Sit with the sick travellers and talk with them, though some would rather be left alone
o.E: Lead the clinic team tonight, even when someone has to wait
o.C: Sort the medicine store so the right dose is quick to find, checking label after label

s14.clue: She sat with the sick through a long night, and tested the well water the next morning.

s15.setup: The square where all the lamps will gather is still bare, and the festival begins at dusk.
s15.line: All the lamps are lit. Let the festival begin!
s15.lit: The square is ready, and its lamp glows over the cobbles.

o.A: Create the welcome arch, though you may still be painting it as the lamps arrive
o.S: Greet newcomers and help them join in, staying by the gate while the fun starts
o.E: Manage the festival stalls, then face the stallholders if sales are slow
o.C: Keep the timetable so every act starts on time, working out of sight all evening

s15.clue: She helped me plan this very festival, and lit the first lamp herself.

chapters.title: The Road Wakes
chapters.line: The first lamps are the hardest. Somewhere on the road, a girl is looking for the lamplighter too.

chapters.title: Hills and Rivers
chapters.line: Every keeper remembers the lamplighter a little differently. A pattern is forming, and the road climbs and bends.

chapters.title: The Salt Wind
chapters.line: You can smell the sea. The lighthouse is close, and its lamp is still dark.

ila.3: Ahead on the road, a girl with a ferry lantern waves. "I am Ila. The lamplighter was my teacher. She left three days ago and nobody knows why. Will you help me find out?"
ila.6: Ila catches up, carrying a flask of lamp oil. "Everyone remembers her differently. A mechanic, a mapmaker, a storyteller. What was she looking for?"
ila.9: Ila points past the hills to the dark sea. "The lighthouse. Still dark, and my flask is nearly empty. It needs every lamp we can light."
ila.last: Ila hands you her lantern. "She told me once the road was never hers. Take mine. I will keep the harbour lamp burning."

meta.noteIntro: Jyo finds a scrap of the lamplighter's note:

intro.text: Once a year, on the Night of Lamps, the valley lights one lamp for every road a person might take. Tonight the hills are glowing.

But the great lighthouse at the end of the road has gone dark. Its lamplighter vanished three days ago, leaving only a torn note: “A lamp burns best for hands that love their work.” Her student Ila is searching for her.
A small firefly named Jyo has guided lamplighters for a hundred years. It finds you on the hill. “The road needs someone to light its lamps,” Jyo whispers. “Will you carry the lantern?”

At every stop, someone needs a hand. You carry two flasks of oil. Spend them on what you would most enjoy doing there: both on one thing, or one on each. There are no right answers. How you light the lamps will show whose road this is.

meta.premise: Once a year, every lamp on the old road is lit and the lighthouse at its end shines out to sea, so that anyone far from home can find the way back. This year the lamplighter has vanished, and her student Ila cannot find out why. Jyo, a firefly who remembers every lamp, has found you.
meta.mission: Walk the road with Ila, help each town in the way you would most gladly spend an evening, and light its lamp. Every keeper remembers the lamplighter a little differently. When enough lamps burn, the lighthouse will shine and show you the doors that open for you.
meta.outro: The lighthouse is lit. Ila's teacher left a last line by its lamp: “The road was never mine. Choose yours.” She never settled on one kind of work. She tried many, so that you could find yours. Whatever you chose along the way, every lamp caught. This is the light you carry.
